$comment: P69 (lane `cs`, D-CSUBSET-GNUC-PREDEFINE-SELECTS-UNIMPLEMENTED-BUILTIN): gcc's checked-arithmetic PREDICATES `__builtin_{add,sub,mul}_overflow_p(a, b, c)`, undeclared until this row: the infinite-precision a OP b cast to the type of `c` -- its own type, unpromoted, or a bit-field's width and signedness -- and whether the cast changed it; nothing is stored, `c`'s side effects are evaluated once, and the call is an integer constant expression when `a` and `b` are (gcc's manual's own enum example, a static initializer, an array bound). Lowered as the same checked HIR arithmetic as `__builtin_add_overflow`, with no store; answered at compile time by the semantic tier when constant. Only gcc has them (clang: `unknown builtin`), so the program asks `__has_builtin` and a compiler without them returns 42 untested; DSS declares them. The exit code is a bitmask of the groups that misbehaved (see main.c). MEASURED 2026-10-01 through `dssharness run probe-reference-cc`, this file: gcc 13.3.0 (runs every check) and clang 18.1.3 at -std=c17 -pedantic-errors and -std=c2x (run 20261001-045021-0bd7a689), mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 in both modes (run 20261001-045047-f73c81d6), MSVC 19.51 (run 20261001-045050-e1233642) and AppleClang 21.0.0 (macos-arm64-release, run 20261001-045100-286c33f9) all exit 42. Every runtime operand derives from argc. The release arm is REPORT-ONLY: its value is that the optimized pipeline neither folds a predicate wrong nor drops the third operand's side effect.
